story.head: The Sabres come in rested
paras: The Blue Jackets won the teams’ first meeting this season, 6-3 in Columbus on Oct 1. The Sabres (7-5-3) lost 2-1 to Ottawa on Wednesday, while the Jackets have won two in a row. Going in, the Blue Jackets are sixth in the Metropolitan (27th in the NHL) and the Sabres seventh in the Atlantic (tied for 18th).

The Blue Jackets get their defensemen shooting (5th), get a lot of their shots blocked (29th) and have a leaky penalty kill (28th). The Sabres, by contrast, get their shots through to the net (4th). They also rarely get pinned in their own end (3rd), but don't block many shots (30th). The Blue Jackets have the edge over the Sabres on forecheck pressure.

Kent Johnson (7 G / 7 A / 14 P in 14 GP) leads the Blue Jackets in scoring, with seven points in his last five games. Charlie Coyle (3 G / 10 A / 13 P in 14 GP) isn’t far behind. For the Sabres, Tage Thompson (10 G / 8 A / 18 P in 15 GP) leads the way in scoring, with nine points in his last five games. Jack Quinn (8 G / 6 A / 14 P in 15 GP) is next in line.
Jet Greaves (2-5-0 / .882 SV% in 7 GS) is expected to start for Columbus, and Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen (4-3-3 / .873 SV% in 9 GS) for Buffalo.
